title: Frantic Assembly - Things I Know To Be True - review
transcript: I saw the touring production of things I know to be true at Nuffield Theatre Southampton it's a tribute to how engrossing it is that I can't remember a quieter audience I mean the stillness was broken only by periodic laughter and at the end widespread sobbing the play presents us with a close loving family comprising middle age parents and their grown-up children their follow revelations about each child and about the parents relationship that stretched the family ties the parents have to come to terms with the fact that once children grow up they're their own people not better versions of themselves as the father puts it your family may not be exactly the same as this one but you will recognize the situation and the relationships there are perhaps too many shocks crammed into two hours but Andrew Beauvoir's writing at times for etiquette others earthy is nearly always believable maybe it's because this is a co-production with State Theatre Company of South Australia but frantic Assembly's trademark physical theater was less evident than I expected and I thought it's a tonne easily with this otherwise riveting naturalistic family drama that I give four stars you
